newsitem.title: ITALY: Rising world banana trade pushes down price-FAO.
newsitem.headline: Rising world banana trade pushes down price-FAO.

text.p: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Wednesday that an expansion in world banana trade had pushed down prices of the tropical fruit.

"Global banana exports have grown by more than 60 percent over the period 1986 to 1995," FAO said in a report to be presented at a three-day intergovernmental conference in Rome which opens on Wednesday.
The agency said 1995 world banana imports totalled 10.6 million tonnes valued at more than $5.3 billion.
"Most of the growth in exports has occurred through increased shipments from Latin America, most notably from Ecuador, Costa Rica and Colombia," the report said.
In Asia, the Philippines had significantly increased its banana exports, while the African states of Cameroon and the Ivory Coast had more than doubled 1986 banana trade levels.

FAO said growth had been fuelled initially by growing demand for bananas in the United States and the European Union (EU) and maintained by the recent opening of Eastern Europe and former Soviet Union markets.

The Rome-based agency said that as a result of the growth in banana supply, world market prices had dipped in recent years. In the United States, the real import price of the fruit had declined 15 percent between 1990-95, it said.
"In general, the market situation is now one of abundant supplies which are putting downward pressure on world banana prices," the report said.
FAO said the drop in prices was hitting developing countries' ability to earn foreign currency revenues from the fruit and many were being forced to diversify.
"Many developing countries depend significantly for their export earnings on the sale of bananas," the report said.
"As the revenue prospects are not expected to improve, the desire of countries dependent on banana exports...to find alternative economic activities has intensified," it added.
The agency said diversification into other commodities such as rubber and palm were under way in Colombia and Ecuador.
